title: Marc Lou's simple tech stack: pick one and never change it
summary: Marc walks through the exact stack behind 30+ sites (Next.js, React, Tailwind, DaisyUI, MongoDB, Vercel, Stripe) and what each tool costs. His core lesson is that stack choice barely matters; sticking with one stack lets you ship faster and make more small bets.

principles.text: Pick one tech stack and never change it; repetition makes you faster at shipping.
principles.quote: pick one text tag and stick to it forever. 3 years ago, I made the decision to never ever change my text tag ever again.

principles.text: Customers don't care about your stack; they care about the problem you solve. Switching stacks wasted years.
principles.quote: I really wish I knew that tech stack don't matter. Your customers really don't care about the invisible. They care about the problem you're solving for them.

principles.text: Shipping faster gets you customers faster, because you can make many small bets.
principles.quote: The more you practice, the more you build apps with the same text, the better I get at it you get. So the faster you'll be able to ship. And the faster you ship, the faster you will get customers

principles.text: Resist trendy new UI libraries; stick with one you like and reuse a base project across products.
principles.quote: This is where people will try to get you to switch to their new trendy UI library. Don't fall for it. Stick to one UI library you like.

principles.text: Keep frontend and API in one serverless project so there are no servers to maintain.
principles.quote: I don't have to uh bother creating a new server. I don't have to uh maintain the server. I don't have to update my server.

principles.text: Build tools to scratch your own itch, like analytics that tie revenue to traffic source.
principles.quote: I wanted to see how does the revenue connects with the traffic.
